criterion: ROADMAP.md M3 criterion 1, second step: the GPU renderer's rtao pass traverses a BVH instead of testing every triangle for every ray, so raw-hall (486,656 triangles) can render with the ray-traced AO channel on a software adapter. Follows evidence/m3-ao-bvh-bounds.json (the CPU reference on the BVH, approved by the coordinator on 2026-10-17).
written: 2026-10-17, before any code and before any run
design: The CPU builds raw::Bvh over the frame's triangles (the same build the CPU reference uses) and uploads two buffers: the nodes (8 floats each: box min, the leaf's first triangle or the interior node's right child, box max, the leaf's count) and the triangles' positions in the BVH's order (9 floats each). The rtao pass walks the tree with a 64-entry stack and the pass's existing hit() test; any-hit only, so the visiting order cannot change the answer. If a ray's stack would overflow, that ray falls back to testing every triangle, so no ray is answered differently. The scan stays as the oracle: Params.rt_bvh = 0 (RAW_NATIVE_AO_ORACLE=scan) runs today's loop, and Params.rt_skew = 1 (RAW_NATIVE_AO_ORACLE=skew) shortens the BVH query by 1% as the control. The raster pass is unchanged. The WGSL is the one source; HLSL and SPIR-V come from scripts/wgsl_to_hlsl.py and glslang as today. The translator itself is not changed.

s1_oracle_gpu.what: the quick identity matrix and the ten glTF models with --gpu, BVH against RAW_NATIVE_AO_ORACLE=scan, on WARP and lavapipe
s1_oracle_gpu.bound: every output file byte-identical (the identity script's timing normalization as usual)

s2_goldens.what: the lavapipe GPU golden (evidence/n3-identity-golden-vulkan-lavapipe.json) and the main CI's GPU checks (WARP --gpu, the WebGPU module on SwiftShader)
s2_goldens.bound: unchanged: the golden compare passes and every verdict is what it was

s3_control.what: RAW_NATIVE_AO_ORACLE=skew on the quick identity matrix
s3_control.bound: at least one output differs from the scan run

s4_overflow.what: how many rays fell back to the scan, counted in a debug readback-free way: a unit test of the flattened tree's depth on raw-hero and raw-hall
s4_overflow.bound: the deepest stack the traversal can need is at most 64 on both assets
s4_overflow.prediction: holds (a binned SAH tree over half a million triangles is about 20 to 40 levels deep)

s5_cost.what: GPU time of the rtao pass is not separately timed; the --gpu run's total GPU time for raw-hero at 320 x 200 with rt on, BVH against scan, on lavapipe in CI
s5_cost.prediction: the BVH run is at least 10 times faster

not_in_this_step: The verified renders of the gallery spheres, raw-hero and raw-hall and the path-traced error per scene (the third step, with its own bounds).
does_not_prove: Anything on a hardware GPU; that the AO estimate is right; anything about the raster pass, which still tests every triangle per pixel.
